stories.headline: China toughens outbound investment rules, expanding scrutiny of overseas tech and data deals

key_facts.fact: China issued new investment rules expanding regulator powers to scrutinize overseas deals involving Chinese investors, technology, and data, effective from July 1, 2026.
The rules follow controversy over Meta's reported moves around Chinese AI startup Manus, which became a flashpoint over outbound technology flows.

stories.headline: Intel details Crescent Island data center GPUs with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X, skipping HBM for inference

key_facts.fact: Intel detailed its Crescent Island data center GPUs at Computex 2026, based on its Xe3P architecture and 'built for agentic AI'.
The Crescent Island GPUs use LPDDR5X memory instead of HBM, with up to 480 GB per accelerator, an unusual choice intended to combat HBM shortages and bring more AI data closer to the chip.

stories.headline: Intel launches Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest CPUs on 18A; claims 30% single-thread lead over AMD Epyc 9965

key_facts.fact: Intel unveiled six Xeon 6+ data center CPU SKUs codenamed Clearwater Forest, marking the first deployment of Intel's 18A process in the data center, with up to 288 cores and 576 MB of L3 cache.
Intel said its new Xeon 6990E+ delivers 30% better single-thread performance and up to 30% more energy efficiency than AMD's 192-core Epyc 9965.
Intel also teased its next-generation Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids on the Intel 18A-P node with PCIe 6.0, 50% more cores and twice the memory bandwidth versus Xeon 6, launching in 2027.

stories.headline: Dutch chip metrology startup Invisix raises EUR 20M seed with tier-one chipmaker backing

key_facts.fact: Netherlands-based Invisix, which is developing advanced chipmaking measurement tools, raised a EUR 20 million seed round.
A 'tier-one' chipmaker participated in the round, which Invisix says will fund work to transform chip metrology.

stories.headline: FT: Iran's military increasingly weaponizes ChatGPT and Gemini for cyber operations

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported that Iran's military and cyber apparatus are increasingly using Western AI tools including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini to support cyber operations, intelligence gathering and military research, citing cybersecurity researchers and Iranian officials.

Iranian-linked actors have used AI systems to improve phishing campaigns, generate malicious code, create convincing online personas and identify vulnerabilities in target networks; researchers said AI has 'lowered the barriers' to cyber operations.
Iranian authorities are also pursuing broader military AI applications including drone technology, electronic warfare and battlefield decision-making systems.

Check Point Research found that the IRGC-affiliated threat actor Nimbus Manticore (UNC1549) leveraged LLM-based tools and AI-assisted development to build new malware including 'MiniFast' during Operation Epic Fury after February 2026 kinetic strikes; Palo Alto Unit 42 tracked 7,381 phishing URLs across 1,881 domains tied to Iranian campaigns through April 2026.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group documented in a February 2026 follow-up that Iran's APT42 used Gemini for reconnaissance and accelerating malware development, and identified HONESTCUE, a malware framework that outsources code generation to Gemini's API via reframed prompts.

stories.headline: Shanghai's MiniMax releases M3, a frontier coding-agent model with 1M-token context and open weights coming

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based MiniMax officially released M3 on June 1, a frontier model aimed at developers building coding agents, long-running automation, and multimodal workflows, with a 1-million-token context window and native image and video input.

MiniMax says M3 scores 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, 66.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 34.8% on SWE-fficiency, 28.8% on KernelBench Hard and 74.2% on MCP Atlas, claiming it beats GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on SWE-Bench Pro while approaching Claude Opus 4.7.
MiniMax says it will publish a technical report and open-source the model weights within 10 days; the model is already available through MiniMax Code, token plans, and API services.

The company's MiniMax Sparse Attention architecture is said to cut per-token compute at one-million-token context to one-twentieth of the prior generation, with more than 9x faster prefill and 15x faster decoding.

MiniMax listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on January 9, 2026, and is positioning M3 to compete with Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's coding agents, and Google's Gemini developer tools through its MiniMax Code agent product.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils Agent Toolkit and Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550B-parameter MoE model built for autonomous agents

key_facts.fact: At GTC Taipei Nvidia unveiled its Agent Toolkit: an open suite of models, blueprints and a secure runtime to help developers turn frontier models into long-running, secure AI agents at scale.

Nemotron 3 Ultra is a 550-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model built for long-running autonomous agents, with up to 5x faster inference speeds and 30% lower running costs versus comparable frontier models in its class, per Nvidia; available June 4 as an NIM microservice via Hugging Face, ModelScope, and OpenRouter.

The core of the toolkit is NemoClaw, a framework providing ready-made templates that structure how agents plan, reason, execute, and delegate tasks; CUDA-X agent skills are available now via the Claude Code marketplace and the Hermes Skills Hub.

Nvidia is also bringing 2x faster local-agent inference across the RTX and DGX lineup via the new OpenShell runtime for Windows and updated llama.cpp/vLLM optimizations, with NemoClaw expanding to all NVIDIA RTX and DGX PCs.

stories.headline: Nvidia launches Cosmos 3, an open physical AI foundation model, and Isaac GR00T humanoid reference

key_facts.fact: On May 31 Nvidia launched Cosmos 3, an open omnimodel for physical AI built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture that combines vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction across text, image, video, ambient sound, and action.

Cosmos 3 Super and Cosmos 3 Nano are available now via build.nvidia.com and Hugging Face, with Cosmos 3 Edge coming for real-time inference; Nvidia says it reduces physical AI training and evaluation cycles from months to days.

Nvidia also unveiled the Isaac GR00T open humanoid reference design powered by its Jetson Thor chip, combining a Unitree H2 Plus robot body with Sharpa five-fingered hands; the company plans to work with humanoid makers in the US, Europe, and South Korea alongside China's Unitree.

A Cosmos Coalition launched alongside the model to advance open world models across industries, with members contributing models, research, and evaluation techniques on Nvidia DGX Cloud infrastructure.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark Arm PC chip with MediaTek; Microsoft uses it in Surface Laptop Ultra

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced the RTX Spark, an Arm-based consumer PC chip family co-developed with MediaTek, pitched as 'the most efficient PC chip ever built'.
RTX Spark offers up to 20 CPU cores and a Blackwell GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores, with up to 128GB of unified memory, capable of '100 FPS 1440p gaming' or running 120B-parameter models locally.
Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra powered by RTX Spark, with a 15-inch mini-LED touchscreen and up to 128GB of unified memory, shipping fall 2026.
Jensen Huang said Microsoft and Nvidia will 'reinvent the PC', starting with 30+ laptops and 10 desktops in the fall from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Acer, Asus, Gigabyte and MSI.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils RTX Spark superchip and DGX Station for Windows, reinventing the PC for AI agents

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced RTX Spark at GTC Taipei at Computex on May 31, calling it a 1-petaflop superchip with full CUDA and RTX stack and up to 128GB of unified memory, built in partnership with MediaTek.
RTX Spark is an Arm-based chip with 20 CPU cores and 6,144 Blackwell GPU cores, capable of running 120-billion-parameter AI agents locally and 100 fps 1440p gaming, in laptops as thin as 14mm.
Over 30 RTX Spark laptops and 10 desktops are coming this fall from Asus, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface, MSI, and Acer; Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra as its flagship.

Nvidia also announced DGX Station for Windows, a deskside AI supercomputer powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra superchip with up to 748GB of coherent memory and 20 petaflops of FP4, capable of running 1-trillion-parameter models locally; coming Q4 2026.
Jensen Huang said Microsoft and Nvidia will 'reinvent the PC' in the era of personal AI, with RTX Spark moving the computer 'from tool to teammate' through Windows-native agents.

stories.headline: Nvidia ramps Vera Rubin into full production with Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX among first Vera CPU users

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced at GTC Taipei that its Vera Rubin platform is ramping into full production with 150 supply-chain partners in Taiwan across 350+ factories in 30 countries; first systems ship this fall.

Vera Rubin delivers 10x agent throughput at scale versus the previous-generation Grace Blackwell platform, unifying NVL72 systems, Vera CPUs, Groq 3 LPX, BlueField-4 STX storage, and Spectrum-6 SPX Ethernet into a single 5-rack 'AI factory' supercomputer.
Jensen Huang said Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are among the first big users for Nvidia's upcoming Vera CPUs, which Nvidia claims run AI workloads 1.8x faster than competing x86 chips.
The Vera Rubin platform introduces Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics, the world's first co-packaged-optics switches with 200Gb/s SerDes, now in production for million-GPU AI factory deployments.

stories.headline: US Army's 'Operation Jailbreak' pushes hacked weapons-system patches to CENTCOM mid-sprint

key_facts.fact: Operation Jailbreak — a 30-day Army-industry sprint at Fort Carson, Colorado that began in early May and concludes June 6 — has involved hundreds of engineers from more than 50 defense companies trying to make legacy and new systems interoperable.

Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has called it 'the largest hackathon in human history' and Army CTO Alex Miller said updates from the first jailbroken systems — including command-and-control tying counter-UAS radars, cameras and effectors together — are already being pushed to US Central Command in the Middle East.

The participating companies include Anduril, Boeing, General Dynamics, L3Harris, Leidos, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, Palantir, Perennial Autonomy and RTX, working under a 'Right to Integrate' (R2I) framework that mandates open APIs.

Driscoll said the initiative was inspired by Ukraine's Delta command operating system, which he saw during a Germany trip; the Iran war 'wrought an urgent need for integrated U.S. defenses against Tehran's deadly, one-way attack drones'.
The hackathon also spurred the Department of Defense's first Application Programming Interface marketplace, where interfaces can be documented and shared for interoperability.

stories.headline: Runway picks London as European HQ, pledges $200M+ for UK AI ecosystem by 2028

key_facts.fact: On June 1 Runway told CNBC it will make London its European headquarters and invest more than $200 million in the UK's AI ecosystem by the end of 2028.
Runway most recently raised $315 million in a Series E led by General Atlantic with AMD Ventures and Nvidia, at a $5.3 billion valuation.
Co-founder and co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis cited proximity to UK customers including the BBC, Fremantle, and WPP, along with London's talent pool, as drivers of the choice.
UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan welcomed the move, saying Runway's London hub will bring world-models research to the UK, helping power breakthroughs from film and gaming to science and robotics.
Runway follows Anthropic (April: London office for 800 staff) and OpenAI (its first permanent UK office) in expanding into London, with Google also moving employees into a new UK HQ this summer.

stories.headline: SoftBank overtakes Toyota as Japan's most valuable company on AI rally

key_facts.fact: SoftBank shares jumped as much as 13% to a record high of 8,546 yen on Monday, pushing the company's market cap to roughly 47-48 trillion yen ($288-306 billion), ahead of Toyota at about 45.7-46 trillion yen after Toyota fell 4.8-4.9%.
SoftBank shares are up more than 80% in 2026, while Toyota shares are down more than 10%.
SoftBank had not surpassed Toyota in market value in more than two decades, since briefly doing so at the peak of Japan's internet bubble in 2000.

Masayoshi Son told La Tribune Dimanche over the weekend that SoftBank would invest 75 billion euros ($87.5 billion) over five years building AI infrastructure in France, calling it 'the largest investment in Europe in infrastructure related to artificial intelligence'.
Japan's Nikkei 225 topped 67,000 for the first time on Monday; SoftBank alone contributed 618 points of the Nikkei's 709-point rise.

SoftBank retains roughly 90% ownership of Arm Holdings, whose shares have more than tripled in 2026; its stake and an OpenAI investment gain drove a quadrupling of annual net profit to over $30 billion.

stories.headline: Index providers rewrite eligibility rules to fast-track SpaceX into S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and Russell 1000

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is heading for a June 12, 2026 Nasdaq debut under the ticker SPCX, with a targeted raise of $75 billion-plus at a $1.5-$2 trillion valuation and an expected public float of only 3%-5%.
Nasdaq approved a fast-entry framework on March 30, 2026, effective May 1, that lets newly-public companies enter the Nasdaq-100 after 15 trading days if they rank within the top 40 holdings by size.

FTSE Russell announced on May 26, 2026 a new fast-track framework letting qualifying large IPOs enter the Russell US Indexes and FTSE GEIS five trading days after listing — widely seen as a 'green lane' for SpaceX, whose investable market cap is projected at about $70 billion post-listing.

S&P Dow Jones opened a consultation in May 2026 proposing to cut the S&P 500 seasoning window from 12 months to 6 months for megacap IPOs and to waive the four-quarter GAAP profitability test above a market-cap threshold — reversing post-dot-com 'Core Earnings' reforms from 2002.

SpaceX reported a Q1 2026 GAAP loss of $4.28 billion and a roughly $2.6 billion FY 2025 loss, making it the most unprofitable firm ever fast-tracked into blue-chip indexes; Starlink contributed $3.26 billion (69%) of Q1 revenue and was the sole profitable segment.

SpaceX structured a phased insider lock-up letting insiders sell up to 20% of locked shares after the first quarterly earnings (covering through June), plus an additional 10% if the stock is trading 30% above the IPO price — a design that helps boost free float quickly to qualify for Nasdaq-100 fast entry.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones strike Saratov refinery and Kirov pumping station; Russia accuses Kyiv of hitting Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed overnight strikes on the Rosneft Saratov oil refinery causing 'a large-scale fire', plus the Lazarevo oil pumping station in Russia's Kirov region — about 1,300 km (800 miles) from Ukrainian-held territory — that serves the Surgut-Gorky-Polotsk pipeline shipping Russian oil to Belarus.

Russia's Defence Ministry said it shot down 216 drones overnight; Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 229 Shahed, Gerbera and Italmas drones at Ukraine, of which 212 were downed and 14 hit their targets at 11 locations.

Russia's state nuclear company Rosatom said a Ukrainian 'kamikaze combat drone' struck the turbine hall of Power Unit No. 6 at the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on Saturday, tearing a hole in the wall; CEO Alexei Likhachev called the attack 'deliberate' but said primary equipment was undamaged.
Ukraine's military denied attacking the Zaporizhzhia plant, calling it 'yet another propaganda ploy', and said it adheres to international humanitarian law.

IAEA head Rafael Grossi said 'attacking nuclear sites is like playing with fire' and the agency's team at the plant requested first-hand access to the affected turbine building; it would be the first drone attack within the plant's perimeter since April 2024.

Ukraine also confirmed strikes on a fuel depot in Matveyev Kurgan (Rostov region), drone command centers in Kalynove (Donetsk region) and Grafovka (Belgorod region), and a drone-assembly workshop in occupied Donetsk; three civilians were injured in Belgorod.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade strikes as Trump tightens terms on draft war-ending MOU

key_facts.fact: The US military said it struck Iranian military sites on Sunday-Monday and Iran's IRGC said it targeted a US base in response; Kuwait reported intercepting missiles and drones — day 94 of the US-Israel war on Iran.

President Trump met with senior aides on Friday to make a 'final determination' on the framework but the meeting ended without a deal, and reports later said he requested fresh changes to the draft text.

The latest draft includes a 60-day cessation of hostilities, a call to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and a framework to resume negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme, per CBS News reporting cited by other outlets.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said no negotiations had taken place on the nuclear file and that ending the war was Tehran's priority; an end to the Lebanon conflict remained 'an essential condition' for any deal.

Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned on state TV that the United States 'was not to be trusted' and that Tehran would not approve any agreement 'until we are certain that the rights of the Iranian people have been upheld'.
Trump posted on Truth Social that 'Iran really wants to make a deal, and it will be a good one for the U.S.A. and those that are with us', adding he was in 'no hurry' to finalize a pact.

Negotiations have run primarily through Pakistani and Qatari mediators rather than direct talks, and it is unclear what role Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei — who has not been seen in public since his succession on March 8 — plays in finalizing the MOU.

stories.headline: Beijing's Vast becomes China's newest AI unicorn with ~$200M raise for AI 3D modeling

key_facts.fact: On June 1 Vast, a Beijing-based AI 3D modeling startup founded in 2023 by 29-year-old gamer Simon Song, said it raised nearly $200 million at a valuation above $1 billion, led by Ince Capital and a China Life Insurance-backed venture fund.
Other investors in the round included Genesis Capital and existing backers Eminence Ventures and Primavera Venture Partners; prior backers include Alibaba and Baidu.

Vast's main product is Tripo Studio, which generates 3D models from text and image prompts for video games, filmmaking, 3D printing, and industrial applications; subscriptions start at $20/month plus per-token usage.

Vast says it has roughly 20 million users globally — with the bulk in the US, followed by Europe, Japan, and South Korea — and counts NetEase and Sony among its enterprise clients; founder Song says the company could turn a profit within two years.
Vast competes with Tencent's Hunyuan 3D and US-based Meshy; Song was a founding member of LLM developer MiniMax before leaving to focus on 3D-asset generation.
